mcat_description.short: Pre Engineered Metal Buildings (PEB) Services covers the end-to-end design, fabrication, supply, and on-site erection of factory-fabricated structural steel building systems, delivered as turnkey or supply-only packages for industrial, commercial, and institutional clients across India.
mcat_description.long: Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEB) are factory-fabricated steel structural systems comprising primary frames (tapered built-up I-section columns and rafters), secondary members (Z/C purlins, girts, eave struts, bracings), and roof/wall cladding panels, all designed off-site and assembled on-site using bolted connections. In India, PEB services are governed by IS 800:2007 (general construction in steel), IS 875 (wind and snow loads), and IS 1893 (seismic design), with design typically executed using STAAD.Pro or equivalent structural analysis software. The service offering ranges from supply-only packages (fabricated components delivered to site) to full turnkey solutions covering concept design, structural engineering, fabrication, transportation, and supervised erection. PEB systems deliver clear spans of 18–90 metres without intermediate columns, construction timelines 40–50% shorter than conventional RCC or conventional steel, and optimised steel usage — making them the default choice for single-storey industrial warehouses, factory sheds, logistics centres, and large-span commercial buildings in India.

market_context: Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEB) in India are factory-fabricated structural steel systems designed to IS 800:2007, IS 875 (Parts 1–3), and IS 1893 (seismic), with many vendors also referencing MBMA (Metal Building Manufacturers Association, USA) and AISC codes for design methodology. The Indian PEB market is dominated by industrial and warehousing applications, with practical clear spans of 18–36m for most warehouses and factories, and 40–60m for aircraft hangars, bus depots, and covered sports facilities. Major Indian PEB vendors include Tata BlueScope, Pennar Industries, Everest Industries, Zamil Steel, EPACK Prefab, and Lloyd Insulations. The procurement process involves issuing an enquiry with building specifications, receiving a frame design proposal and erection drawings, and a quote covering dead load, live load, and wind analysis per IS 875 — with erection typically by the manufacturer's sub-contractors and a lead time of 8–12 weeks from order to delivery. India's industrial and warehousing sector is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10–12% through 2027 (ICRA), with Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities driving approximately 40% of new demand (CII) — making PEB the default construction method for single-storey industrial buildings. Crane-compatible PEB (overhead cranes up to 50T, IS 807 duty class) is a significant sub-segment commanding a cost premium. The 'Services' framing of this MCAT reflects that buyers procure PEB as a complete design-fabricate-erect service engagement, not as a commodity product.
